channel.description: Latest articles from West Hawaii Today (westhawaiitoday.com)

item.title: Public invited to 5 “Coffee With a Cop” events in West Hawaii.
item.description: As part of its ongoing community outreach to listen to community members, the Hawaii Police Department is holding five “Coffee With a Cop” events in the Kona area this month in order for the public to get to know their district police officers.

item.title: Applicants sought for pool lifeguard positions
item.description: The Hawaii County Department of Parks and Recreation is now accepting applications for summer lifeguard positions at county pools.

item.title: BIIF boys soccer: Oda, Chung lead All-League selections
item.description: The Big Island Interscholastic Federation (BIIF) released its All-League teams for the 2025-26 boys soccer season Tuesday, highlighting another exciting season of premier play on the pitch.

item.title: Stephen Tsai: Hawaii jersey retirement ‘a big deal to me,’ Anthony Carter says
item.description: Anthony Carter never dared to dream of the life he is now living.

item.title: Hawaii defeats Gonzaga in a wild finish to win opening series
item.description: With Manoa Valley theatrics, Elijah Ickes sprinted home on a wild pitch in the ninth inning to deliver the Hawaii baseball team a 4-3 victory over Gonzaga before 2,238 at Les Murakami Stadium.

item.title: Civil rights champion Jesse Jackson dies at 84
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Charismatic U.S. civil rights leader Jesse Jackson, an eloquent Baptist minister raised in the segregated South who became a close associate of Martin Luther King Jr and twice ran for the Democratic presidential nomination, has died at age 84, his family said in a statement on Tuesday.

item.title: State lawmakers try to tackle Hawaii’s teacher shortage
item.description: A measure that would create a new five-year state permit for visiting international teachers has drawn strong support from the state Department of Education as well as immigrant and educator advocates, as Hawaii continues to grapple with a persistent teacher shortage.

item.title: Kona coffee worker back home after ICE arrest
item.description: A 42-year-old Captain Cook man who was locked up more than five months by the federal government without charges or bond was freed late last month, the American Civil Liberties Union of Hawaii said Tuesday.

item.title: The price of admission to Epstein’s world: Silence
item.description: When Jeffrey Epstein said “massage” in the years after he got out of jail in 2009, what did his friends and associates think he meant? Epstein had been convicted in a Florida court of sex crimes with minors in 2008. His method, reported in The New York Times at the time, had been to recruit girls as young as 14 to his home and persuade them to undress and massage him. Then he would force them to have sex and paid them cash.

item.title: Allegations in Epstein files may amount to ‘crimes against humanity,’ UN experts say
item.description: Millions of files related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein suggest the existence of a “global criminal enterprise” that carried out acts meeting the legal threshold of crimes against humanity, according to a panel of independent experts appointed by the United Nations Human Rights Council.
